full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff-respondent instituted Other Suit No.231 of 1969 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Sadar, Chittagong, for ejectment of the defend-ant-appellant and recovery of the arrear rents. Plaintiff's case in brief was that he purchased the suit premises from the former owner and he demanded rents from the defendant from Chaitra, 1374 B.S., by a notice dated 27-7-1968. The defendant in order to avoid payment of rent filed a case before the House Rent Controller for depositing the rent. The plaintiff served a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act terminating the tenancy. His case was that defendant was a defaulter from Chaitra 1374 B.S. to Jaistha, 1375 B.S. As the defendant failed to vacate the premises the plaintiff filed the present suit. The defendant contested the suit contending, inter alia, that he paid rent in advance to the vendor of the plaintiff upto Jaistha, 1375 B.S. and as such he is not a defaulter as alleged in the plaint and that he had been depositing the rent from Ashar, 1376 B.S. to the House Rent Controller. 

 3. The trial Court decreed the suit, holding that the defendant is a defaulter in payment of rents from Chaitra, 1374 B.S. to Jaistha, 1375 B.S. and that the notice was validly served upon the, defendant. The defendant preferred Other Appeal No.145 of 1971 and the learned Subordinate Judge 3rd Court, Chittagong, who heard the appeal, reversed the decision of the trial Court and dismissed the suit. The plaintiff then preferred Second Appeal No.499 of 1972 and a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division allowed the appeal, set aside the decision of the lower appellate Court and restored the decision of the trial Court. 

 4. Leave was granted to consider whether in view of Ext. F series the defendant had defaulted in depositing rents in accordance with the provision of section 18(5) and section 19 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance. The defend-ant filed rent receipts Exts. B series showing payment of rent from the month of Chaitra, 1374 B.S. to Jaistha, 1375 B.S. The defendant also filed Challans Ext. F series to show that he deposited rents with the House Rent Controller for the months of Bhadra, 1376 B.S. to Chaitra, 1377 B.S. 

 5. Mr. M.H. Khandker, learned Counsel, appearing for the appellant argued that the lower appellate Court found Ext. B series genuine documents and the learned Judge of the High Court Division having accepted the same committed an error in making out a new case holding that the Chalan Ext. F series showing payment of rent with the House Rent Controller would show that the defendant had defaulted in payment of rent in accordance with the provisions of section 18(5) read with section 19 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance. He further argued that the learned Judge of the High Court Division misapplied the case of Ramjan Ali Mistry V. Md. Hedayetullah, 31 D.L.R. (A.D.) 183. 

 6. Mr. B.B. Roy Chowdhury, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the respondent argued that in view of the finding of the learned Judge that the defendant failed to prove deposit of rents with the House Rent Controller in accordance with the provisions of section 18(5) read with section 19 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, the appellant had become a defaulter and as such, he was not entitled to the protection under section 18 of the Ordinance. He argued that the rents paid by Challans Ext. F series as produced by the defendant was not in accordance with law. 

 7. The learned Judge of the High Court Division accepted rent receipts Ext. B series showing payment of rents for the months of Chaitra, 1374 B.S. to Jaistha, 1375 B.S. but he found that the rents covered by the Challans Ext. F series were paid not within 15 days as prescribed by the Ordinance but several days after due date. 

 8. The tenancy was terminated with the expiry of the month of Ashar, 1376 B.S. and in accordance with the provision of section 18(5) and section 19 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, to avail the protection against ejectment, the tenant was required to deposit rents 

 9. The protection given under law against ejectment of a tenant is available as long as he paid rent in accordance with law. 

 10. It is the positive finding of the High Court Division that deposit of rent by Challans Ext. F series is not in accordance with law, to entitle the defendant to the aforesaid protection. 

 11. Relevant provisions of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance are as follows:- 

 "18(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, or the Contract Act, 1872, no order or decree for the recovery of possession of any pre-mises shall be made as long as the tenant pays rent to the full extent allowable by this Ordinance and perform the conditions of the tenancy: 

 (5) No tenant shall be entitled to the benefit of this section in respect of any premises unless, he pays the rent due by him in respect of such premises to the full extent allowable by this Ordinance within the time fixed in the contract with his landlord or, in the absence of such contract, by the fifteenth day of the month next following that for which the rent is payable, of in the cases provided for in section 19, unless the tenant has deposited such rent or any subsequent rent in respect of such premises as provided in that section together with, in the case mentioned in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of that section, the cost of transmission referred to in that clause within the time specified in that section."19(1) Deposit of rent by the tenant in certain circumstance.—When a landlord refuses to accept any rent referred to in section 18 remitted by postal money order by a tenant in respect of any premises, the tenant may— 

 (a) deposit such rent within a fortnight of the date on which the rent so remitted is returned to the tenant by the postal authorities as undelivered, and 

 (b) unless the landlord signifies by notice in writing to the tenant his willingness to accept any subsequent rent which becomes due in respect of such premises, also deposit such subsequent rent within a fort-night of the date on which such rent becomes due, from the expiry of the time within which such rent is required to be paid under sub-section (5) of section 18 together with the cost of transmission by postal money order of the money deposited to the landlord." 

 "The tenant must pay rent in terms of the contract and in the absence of the contract within 15th day the next following month on which the rent falls due and if the landlord refuses to accept the rent tendered by the tenant, the tenant must remit the rent within the aforesaid 15th day of the following month by Money Order. If the rent remitted by Money Order is refused the tenant can deposit the rent with the House Rent Controller within a fortnight from the date of the receipt of the undelivered rent sent through the postal authority and when these conditions as prescribed in the Ordinance are fulfilled by the tenant, he gets the protection, otherwise the protection from ejectment on ground of default in payment of rent granted by the Ordinance is clearly taken away by the express language of sub-section (5) of section 18." 

 Following the aforesaid principle, High Court Division held that in accordance with provision of section 18(5) and section 19 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, the tenant is required to continue to deposit rents in accordance with law to avail of the protection against ejectment. The tenant in the instant case was required under law to deposit rents of every month within 15th of the following month even after termination of the tenancy. 

 13. The learned Judge of the High Court Division on consideration of evidence on record came to the finding that "the defendant having failed to pay or deposit rents according to the provision of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance for the months of Bhadra 1375 B.S. and for some subsequent months as indicated in Exhibits F(1), F(6) and F(24) and F(35), he is not entitled to any protection against ejectment and thus he is a defaulter in payment of rents." The learned Judge has given cogent reason for his finding and has rightly applied the principle laid down by this Court in the case of Ramjan Ali V. Md. Hedayetullah. We find no merit in this appeal which is dismissed with costs.
